During its June 8 broadcast of “Freestyle Live: Special Edition,” which aired from 7 to 9 p.m. Eastern on the company’s Facebook Live page ( facebook.com/drewestatecigar ) and YouTube channel ( youtube.com/drewestatecigar ), Drew Estate revealed the secret identity of the mystery cigar inside its latest Freestyle Live Event Pack … the all-new Liga Privada H99 Connecticut Corojo Papas Fritas (115mm x 44). Liga Privada H99 Connecticut Corojo Papas Fritas marries two of Drew Estate’s most popular cigar concepts—its exclusive hybrid H99 Connecticut Corojo capa leaf and the Papas Fritas vitola. Since its debut more than a decade ago, the distinctive Papas Fritas vitola has become one of the most beloved Liga Privada Único Serie cigars due to its quick smoke format, making it the ideal choice for on-the-go cigar lovers who want to savor a rich Liga Privada cigar. Working side-by-side with H99’s exclusive tobacco farmer, Drew Estate has slowly increased its yield, year-over-year to expand the rare H99 tobacco’s availability. The hybrid H99 Connecticut Corojo capa is born from a union of Stalk-Cut Habano and Connecticut Corojo seeds to produce a luxurious tobacco. A robust Mexican San Andres Otapan Negro Último Corte capote contrasts perfectly with the H99 capa; and dense and earthy well-aged Nicaraguan, Honduran and Pennsylvania Green River One Sucker tripa tobaccos complete Liga Privada H99 Connecticut Corojo Papas Fritas’ complex and deceptively full-bodied blend. The all-new Liga Privada H99 Connecticut Corojo Papas Fritas will be available exclusively at participating Drew Diplomat Program partners beginning on June 9. Packaged in 25-count boxes, the cigars’ MSRP is $7.50 per cigar or $187.50 per box.

Drew Estate introduces the Liga Privada Unico Serie Bakkwa, a cigar crafted to honor Lunar New Year traditions, exclusively available through CoH Cigars in Hong Kong. This full-bodied Churchill-sized cigar features a Connecticut Stalk Cut wrapper, delivering a robust, complex flavor profile, designed to echo the festive Lunar New Year spirit. Inspired by the Chinese delicacy Bakkwa, a symbol of good fortune and prosperity, this cigar aims to blend cultural significance with a luxurious smoking experience. Jonathan Drew, Founder and Presidente of Drew Estate highlights “I’m inspired by Bakkwa’s role as a cultural bridge, encapsulating festivity and indulgence in the form of a premium cigar. Drew Estate is so diverse as a company and as a brand, our people and our philosophies. Our zest for life and passion is embodied beautifully in this new offering. It’s dope.” Presented in 12-count boxes, the Liga Privada Unico Serie Bakkwa is priced at retail of $235 per box. Bakkwa is a nod to the Unico Serie’s tradition of pork-themed cigars, poised to be a coveted item for Hong Kong’s cigar enthusiasts.

Crowned Heads is showing a new cigar by Luciano and Ace Prime Cigars called the Fiat Lux. The name comes from Genesis and the phrase “let there be light”. According to the company, when you taste a great blend you can be enlightened by delving into the complexity of the flavors and with the possibility of introspection as you enjoy the smoke. Fiat Lux is a blend that generates that deliberation. As a result, the four sizes are named for the mindful journey. They are Insights 5.625” X 46, Intuition at 5” X 50, Genius measuring 5.5” x 52 and Acumen at 6 X 56. The blend is a high priming of Ecuador Sumatran for the wrapper, over Nicaraguan Pueblo Nuevo binder and fillers from Nicaragua — Condega, Ometepe and Jalapa. The cigars come in 20 count boxes with prices ranging from $8.75 to $10.75

Luciano Cigars is excited to announce the launch of Chicos, a new size of the acclaimed UNDERRATED by Luciano Cigars. A 4 x 40 cigar tailored for brisk winter outings and those seeking a high-quality, quick smoke. Designed with the same attention to detail and superior blend as their flagship offerings, Chicos is crafted to deliver robust flavor in a compact, convenient format. Engineered for the outdoors, Chicos features their celebrated long-filler blend composed of Connecticut Broadleaf fillers, Ecuadorian HVA, and Pueblo Nuevo tobaccos, all enveloped in a classic San Andres wrapper. Packaged in a 50-count box and priced at an attractive MSRP of only $6, this cigar combines exceptional value with uncompromised quality. While some have playfully dubbed it the “Dog Walker” cigar, they proudly call it Chicos—a nod to its approachable, spirited character. Chicos is not only launching now but is also available for immediate shipment. Their warehouse is fully stocked, and their most preferred retailers are already receiving their orders. Pre-releases in Luciano Cigars branded lounges and through their preferred partners have paved the way for a smooth, enthusiastic market entry.

Macanudo is expanding its sophisticated Emissary lineup with a new cigar featuring rare tobacco grown near Bordeaux, France. The star of the release is French tobacco cultivated in the Mugron River Valley, where it is nurtured by the Atlantic sea breeze. Emissary France is crafted with an Ecuadorian Habano Wrapper (10-Year Aged), a USA Broadleaf Binder (10-Year Aged), and a filler blend composed of Dominican Piloto (10-Year Aged), USA Broadleaf (8-Year Aged), Brazilian Arapiraca (7-Year Aged) and French (4-Year Aged). The Emissary series was created to showcase rare and distinctive European tobaccos, and Emissary France is no exception. Following the critically acclaimed debut of Emissary España, this latest release furthers Macanudo’s commitment to crafting cigars that highlight the elegance and depth of unique terroirs. Emissary España featured tobacco grown in Riolobos, Spain. Matt Wilson, Senior Brand Manager for Macanudo, said, “After the success of Emissary España, we knew we had high expectations to meet. Going to France, with its incredible flavors and deep-rooted tradition of sophistication, felt like a natural next step. We were inspired by the richness and refinement that define French craftsmanship and set out to create a cigar that embodies those same qualities. Emissary France is the perfect expression of that vision, delivering an experience that is both refined and unforgettable.” Handcrafted at HATSA, Macanudo Emissary France is a full-time release available in four vitolas. All sizes come in 16-count boxes. Emissary France will begin shipping to stores March 3, 2025. Macanudo Emissary France Robusto (5” x 52) – SRP per cigar $14.99 Macanudo Emissary France Toro (6” x 52) – SRP per cigar $15.99 Macanudo Emissary France Churchill (7” x 48) – SRP per cigar $16.99 Macanudo Emissary France Perfecto (5 ¾” x 50) – SRP per cigar $17.99

Macanudo Inspirado Green will launch its fourth frontmark in February with a large format cigar called Gigante. At 6 x 60, Gigante will round out the Inspirado Green line which debuted 2020 and currently consists of a Robusto, Toro and Churchill. Laurel Tilley, brand ambassador of Macanudo said, “Macanudo Inspirado Green Gigante brings together the unique experience of Brazilian tobacco with one of the cigar industry’s most in-demand sizes. We’re confident that this new and distinctive smoke will deliver increased excitement to the top-selling Macanudo brand.” Handcrafted at General Cigar Dominicana in Santiago, D.R., Macanudo Inspirado Green is a medium-bodied collection that features hand-selected tobaccos from four countries. A rich Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper serves as the foundation of the blend. Beneath an Indonesian binder is a blend of Dominican and Colombian filler leaves that mingle with the wrapper to create a full-flavored, medium-bodied smoke brimming with earth and pepper. Macanudo Inspirado Green Gigante will ship to retailers on February 15, 2022 and will come in boxes containing 20 cigars. SRP per cigar USD 8.29.

The Macanudo Inspirado White line is expanding with two new sizes. Steve Abbot, senior brand manager of Macanudo said, “The Macanudo Inspirado White portfolio had consisted of six popular sizes, yet our retailers and cigar smokers wanted more. We responded by creating a Corona and Cigarillo and are confident that the new sizes will become fast-selling additions to this highly successful brand.” Introduced in 2017, Macanudo Inspirado White is counted among the top-sellers in the Macanudo portfolio. Macanudo Inspirado White is made with a proprietary Ecuadoran Connecticut wrapper developed by General Cigar’s agronomists. Aged for six years and refined to a creamy shade of gold, the wrapper crowns an Indonesian binder. The blend features Nicaraguan Condega and Mexican San Andres leaves, each aged for four years and Nicaraguan Jalapa aged for two years. Both new formats have begun shipping to retailers. The Corona is handcrafted at HATSA in Danli, Honduras and the Cigarillo is made at General Cigar Dominicana in Santiago, D.R. Macanudo Inspirado White Corona (5.5” x 42) – SRP per cigar $5.49; 20 cigars per box Macanudo Inspirado White Cigarillo (4 3/16” x 32) – SRP per 10-cigar tin $15.99.

The world’s first Vintage cigar was created by Macanudo more than 40 years ago to spotlight an exceptional wrapper produced in part by Mother Nature. The Vintage tradition marches on with Macanudo Vintage Maduro 2013. The five-country blend reflects optimal climatic conditions and calls upon meticulous curing and precise maturation techniques perfected by the artisans of Macanudo. The 2013 growing season saw some of the highest temperatures on record in the Connecticut River Valley, with soaring humidity and optimal rainfall that yielded an exceptionally brawny Broadleaf tobacco. Cured and aged for an entire decade to bring forth an array of undeniably diverse notes on the palate, this singular tobacco makes its debut in Macanudo Vintage 2013. Ernest Gocaj who oversees the Connecticut growing operations for Macanudo said, “The growing season in 2013 was one of the best I’ve ever seen. The crop was exceptional at harvest, which meant that we had to be obsessive when it came to monitoring the tobacco during the eight-week curing process. That’s how important curing is. Our hard work paid off because we ultimately brought the tobacco’s very best attributes to life.” A master blender’s assortment of tobaccos complement this exceptional wrapper to create the rich indulgence that is Macanudo Vintage 2013. The filler is made up of Dominican Piloto Cubano from two different primings, along with Brazilian Mata Fina and Nicaraguan Jalapa. The binder is Honduran OSA. Macanudo Vintage 2013 is shipping to retailers July 3 and will be released in three sizes, each chosen to enhance the superlative blend. The cigars are individually encased in cedar wrapping and are presented in handmade, solid wood boxes that protect 20 expertly-crafted cigars, each made by artisans at General Cigar Dominicana in Santiago, DR. Robusto (5” x 50); SRP per cigar $11.99 Toro Grande (6” x 54); SRP per cigar $12.99 Churchill (7 x 49); SRP per cigar $13.29

The world’s first Vintage cigar was created by Macanudo nearly 40 years ago to spotlight an exceptional wrapper developed in part by Mother Nature herself. Today, the Vintage tradition continues with Macanudo Vintage 2010. The 2010 growing season saw the highest temperatures in 25 years in the Connecticut River Valley, with high humidity and optimal rainfall that yielded an exceptionally silky shade-grown wrapper tobacco. Cured and aged for an entire decade, this singular tobacco makes its debut in Macanudo Vintage 2010. Ernest Gocaj who oversees the Connecticut growing operations for Macanudo said, “We could not have asked for a better growing season than we had in 2010. Yet this is only part of the story. After such a beautiful crop is harvested, the hard work begins again because the most critical process for growing tobacco is curing. Given how unique and special this crop was, we were obsessive in monitoring the tobacco throughout the eight-week curing process, and ultimately brought its very best attributes to life.” A deeply-aged assortment of tobaccos complement this wrapper. The blend features Dominican Piloto Cubano 94, a proprietary Cuban-seed varietal regenerated by General Cigar’s agronomists over a ten-year process. The Dominican Piloto Cubano 94 is married to Nicaraguan and Honduran leaves, aged three and five years, respectively. The blend is bound with a Honduran leaf. Macanudo Vintage 2010 will be released on August 17 in three sizes. The cigars are presented in handmade, solid wood boxes. Toro Grande (6 5/8 x 54); SRP per cigar USD 11.99 Torpedo (6 1/4 x 52); SRP per cigar USD 11.99 Churchill (7 1/4 x 48); SRP per cigar USD 12.29

The Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua is now available in a 52 x 4 ½ size, the “Exclusivo.” The size – created exclusively for Casa de Montecristo’s retail stores and lounges – is now available. Like its predecessor, the Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua Exclusivo pays tribute to the original 1935 blend that made Montecristo the icon it is today. To fully honor Montecristo and the original tobaccos used in that first Montecristo cigar, Rafael Nodal, AJ Fernandez and the Grupo de Maestros worked to find a precise and exquisite proprietary blend of aged tobaccos. “At Casa de Montecristo,” said CEO Brad Winstead, “we are continuously looking for ways to offer our adult clientele the highest quality premium products. The Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua Exclusivo is a perfect fit for our brand and we look forward to providing our guests with this exclusive size. We are honored to be able to offer cigar lovers something they can’t get anywhere else.” The Montecristo 1935 Anniversary Nicaragua Exclusivo is offered in 10-count boxes and priced at an MSRP of $15.00 per cigar. Limited quantities will be available for purchase starting June 11 exclusively, as noted above, at Casa de Montecristo. Size and Frontmark: 52 x 4 1/2, Exclusivo Price: USD 15.00 Origin: Nicaragua

Odyssey is adding a bold, new line to its accessibly-priced portfolio with Odyssey Full. The five-cigar collection of Nicaraguan-made smokes rounds out the Odyssey portfolio with a rich, fuller-bodied profile and marks the sixth collection of Odyssey cigars. Odyssey Full is handcrafted by artisans at STG Estelí in Nicaragua. The blend is centered on Cuban seed tobaccos and features a high concentration of ligero leaves from Nicaragua and Colombia in the blend for a memorable smoking experience. With a Nicaraguan Habano binder and Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper, Odyssey Full delivers a robust yet balanced smoke that’s earthy and spicy with a hint of leather on the finish. Ed Lahmann, senior brand manager for Odyssey said, “Given its accessible price point, Odyssey Full is a great option for the tried and true cigar smoker who’s looking to add variety to their go-to set of brands. We’re confident that this new line is going to catch fire quickly.” Shipping this month, Odyssey Full will be available in these five sizes, each in 20-count boxes: Gigante (6 x 60); SRP per cigar USD 2.69 Churchill (7 x 48); SRP per cigar USD 2.49 Toro (6 x 50); SRP per cigar USD 2.19 Corona (5 1/2 x 42); SRP per cigar USD 1.69 Robusto (5 x 50); SRP per cigar USD 1.89

Partagas is launching Cortado, the brand’s first Connecticut Shade-wrapped offering and the first Partagas line to be handcrafted by artisans in Nicaragua. The new, four-cigar collection has just begun shipping to retailers. Matt Wilson, senior brand manager for Partagas said, “With interest in the Partagas brand continuing to grow, we felt it was the right time to expand the brand portfolio with a mellow-to-medium-bodied blend. The team and I are especially proud of Partagas Cortado’s incredible versatility when it comes to pairing. The blend is creamy and complex, and its taste notes can push forward or bow to other flavors, depending on the pairing. We feel our Nicaraguan artisans did a wonderful job with the blend and look forward to sharing it with Partagas fans, old and new.” Handcrafted at STG Estelí in Nicaragua, Partagas Cortado is wrapped in a silky Ecuadoran-grown Connecticut Shade wrapper and features an Indonesian binder over a blend of Honduran Jamastran and San Andres tobacco, with Nicaraguan Condega and Jalapa. Cortado is presented in wooden wrap-set boxes that align with the aesthetic of Partagas Black Label and Yellow. The blend is being released in four sizes to complement a range of smoking occasions. Corona (5 1/2 x 42) – SRP per cigar USD 6.39 (20 cigars per box) Robusto (5 x 50) – SRP per cigar USD 7.19 (20 cigars per box) Toro (6 x 52) – SRP per cigar USD 7.59 (20 cigars per box) Presidente (8 x 54) – SRP per cigar USD 8.99 (10 cigars per box)

Tabacalera Perdomo announced the release of the new Perdomo Reserve 10th Anniversary Box-Pressed Maduro and Sun Grown in August 2020. The Perdomo Reserve 10 th Anniversary Champagne, awarded Best Brand Nicaragua in 2018 by Cigar Journal, continues to be one of the top-selling premium cigars on the market and the new Maduro and Sun Grown are sure to compliment the line and capture the hearts of cigar enthusiasts worldwide. “Our Perdomo Reserve line has been on the market for over 20 years. We wanted to come out with something really special to honor the history of the brand and offer a cigar that every cigar smoker would truly fall in love with,” states Nick Perdomo, Jr., President, and CEO. “We blended these cigars with 6-year aged Cuban-seed wrapper, binder, and filler tobaccos that we carefully hand-selected from our most prestigious farms located in the Estelí, Condega, and the famed Jalapa Valley in Nicaragua. We blended these cigars to not only be rich in flavor, but also to be very smooth on the pallet with slight hints of sweetness. Our tasting panel with over 250 years of cigar making and premium tobacco experience was amazed at how great this blend tastes.” The Perdomo Reserve 10 th Anniversary Box-Pressed Maduro is a medium to full-bodied Nicaraguan “puro” blended with a dark, oily 6-year old Cuban-seed Nicaraguan wrapper that has been bourbon barrel-aged for an additional 14 months and is paired with 6-year old Cuban-seed Nicaraguan binder and filler tobaccos to create naturally sweet flavors with hints of dark cocoa and espresso on the finish. The Perdomo Reserve 10 th Anniversary Box-Pressed Sun Grown is a medium to full-bodied Nicaraguan “puro” blended with a beautiful 6-year old Cuban-seed Nicaraguan wrapper that has been bourbon barrel- aged for an additional 10 months and is paired with 6-year old Cuban-seed Nicaraguan binder and filler tobaccos to create a rich core of earthy flavors with hints of spice and sweetness on the finish. The Ace Prime completes the trilogy of the Clasico line. Firstly with Pichardo Clasico Toro, with a Sumatra wrapper; then Pichardo Clasico Maduro with a Brazilian wrapper (recently Launched on Nov 2020) – now, the classic line receives a new addition: The Pichardo Clasico Natural. Pichardo Clasico Natural Size:61/2x 50 Wrapper: Habano Sun Grown Ecuador Binder: Nicaragua Fillers: Nicaragua MSRP: $ 9.00 *Shipping on March 2021 “The Pichardo Clasico Natural is the fruit of a master craftsman – producing a medium cigar full of flavor, smooth, and perfectly balanced. The amazing result is not a surprise for us. Pichardo is a fourth-generation tobacconist: heir to more than a century and a half of knowledge in the world of tobacco,” says Luciano Meirelles (Co-Founder ACE Prime and Tabacalera Pichardo). “It was a difficult journey, but we knew this cigar needed to be very special to complete the trilogy of the Clasico line,” Eradio Pichardo (Co-Founder ACE Prime and Tabacalera Pichardo).

Previously released in limited quantities every year, Rare Corojo is now a regular-production cigar within the Punch portfolio. In addition, Punch is also launching a new, limited-edition Rare Corojo size just for 2025. That cigar, a Box Pressed El Gordo (6 X 60), features the same blend as prior Rare Corojo limited-production releases. Rare Corojo includes an extra-rich Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper with a distinctive reddish hue and uniquely smooth taste. It has a Connecticut Broadleaf binder and Honduran, Nicaraguan, and Dominican Piloto Cubano filler tobaccos. Punch’s brand manager, Scott Abney, said, “For years, Punch fans have clamored for more Rare Corojo, and we’re excited to deliver it to them as a regular-production line. The classic blend will be available across nine frontmarks in addition to the limited-edition Box Pressed El Gordo for 2025. You’ve waited patiently for this day to arrive; now it’s time to celebrate with a Rare Corojo or two.” Punch Rare Corojo is produced at the STG Danlí factory in Honduras. The limited-edition Box Pressed El Gordo will begin shipping in early January, and it contains 20 cigars per box. (Note: some Rare Corojo sizes contain 20 cigars per box, while others have 25, and the Rothschild frontmark includes 50 cigars per box.) Noel Rojas, recently featured in Cigar Journal’s Spring 2026 issue, continues to build a reputation as the “King of the Small Gauges,” favoring slimmer vitolas that emphasize wrapper-driven complexity. “We focus on smaller ring gauges because over 80 percent of a cigar’s flavor comes from the wrapper,” Rojas says, presenting his new Quiet Morning cigar. Though wrapped in Connecticut leaf, its blend of Nicaraguan and Dominican Ligero delivers a medium-to-full-bodied profile that defies the category’s milder expectations. Also debuting at PCA 2026 is the limited-edition Cinco de Mayo, featuring seven-year-aged Connecticut broadleaf filler, a Nicaraguan binder, and an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, an indication of Rojas’s continued focus on depth and balance. His booth in New Orleans maintained a steady buzz, reflecting a boutique brand clearly on the rise.

The next Firecracker will be a limited release for 2016 and as usual it will be released just before the 4th of July. This year’s production will be The CroMagnon Firecracker from RoMa Craft Tobac out of the Nica Sueno factory in Esteli Nicaragua. The CroMagnon Firecracker will measure 3.5” x 50, using a U.S. Connecticut Broadleaf Maduro Wrapper. The filler leaf for the new CroMagnon blend was acquired from three separate growing regions in Nicaragua: Esteli, Condega and a small farm north of Esteli on the Honduran border. The blend is expected to be full bodied and full flavored. There will be just 200 boxes made with 20 Firecracker Cigars in each box all adorning the CroMagnon name. The first Firecracker cigar was released on May 19, 2007 at a cigar rolling event at Two Guys Smoke Shop in New Hampshire featuring Jose Don “Pepin” Garcia. David Garofalo, owner and founder of Two Guys Smoke Shop asked Pepin to roll him a short cigar and to put a long pig tail on it. Pepin followed the direction and The Firecracker Cigar was born. Over the years limited releases of The Firecracker Cigars were made and most commonly released near the 4th of July and made by various cigar manufacturers. Past Firecracker Cigars include Don Pepin and Tatuaje (M80) at My Fathers Cigar Factory, Jose Dominguez, Iconic Leaf, at Leyendas Cubanas and La Flor Dominicana. The filler leaf for the new CroMagnon blend was acquired from three separate growing regions in Nicaragua: Esteli, Condega and a small farm north of Esteli on the Honduran border. Prices for the 2016 CroMagnon Firecracker are expected to be $119.99 per box of 20 ($6.99 a cigar) and available only at Two Guys Smoke Shop sometime in late June or early July.

Romeo y Julieta 1875 Connecticut Nicaragua is the latest expansion of the premium cigar line. As the name implies, the Romeo y Julieta 1875 Connecticut Nicaragua is a blend of Nicaraguan tobaccos, but this special collaboration with Plasencia Cigars includes tobaccos from the family’s own private reserves. The cigar is wrapped in a Connecticut seed leaf grown in Nicaragua and aged more than three years. Connecticut seed wrapper – originally from the rocky, rich soil of New England in the United States – is now harvested in other key cigar regions of the world, such as Ecuador and Honduras. Continuing to expand flavors and characteristics of their tobaccos, the Plasencia family began growing Connecticut seed tobaccos in Honduras and Nicaragua. Rafael Nodal, Head of Product Capability for Tabacalera USA, collaborated for almost two years with the Plasencia family in creating this cigar. “Getting to work with the Plasencia family on this cigar which uses a Connecticut seed wrapper grown in Nicaragua, is for me an honor. Having the opportunity to take the Romeo y Julieta consumer on a journey of discovering new flavors and new experiences, is a real privilege,” Nodal said. “This cigar is intriguing,” he explained. “It’s not a Connecticut cigar, nor is it a Nicaragua cigar. It is the first Connecticut-Nicaragua Cigar. And that makes for a big difference.” The Romeo Y Julieta 1875 Connecticut Nicaragua will be available in four sizes. The cigar will be available in a Toro (52 x 6), Bully (50 x 5), Magnum (60 x 6) and Churchill (50 x 7). The price of the cigar will range from $7.20 to $8.35.

The redux of Room101 Hit & Run will soon hit retail, with the new blend created by the dynamic duo of Matt Booth and Robert Caldwell. Matt Booth said, “I’m thrilled to bring another Room101 sub-brand back to life with this expression of Hit & Run. The brand was born of a collaborative seed between myself and Robert Caldwell. It’s about our creative process as much as it is about two-like minded psychopaths who’ve stuck together over the years. This cigar is the physical and combustible manifestation of an intergalactic connection which proves that an authentic friend and a good cigar can help more than you may imagine.” The blend is made with a Mexican San Andres wrapper, an Ecuadorian Sumatra binder and a blend of Nicaraguan C-98 and Pennsylvania filler with an added layer of Nicaraguan leaf. Matt Booth describes the experience as being “sophisticated with depth and transition,” and notes that it “blends power with balance.” He says Hit & Run “pairs well with your favorite memory of the DMV.” The line is crafted at William Ventura in Tamboril, DR, where four frontmarks have been made: Robusto (5” x 50); SRP per cigar $12.99 Toro (6” x 50); SPR per cigar $13.29 Gordo (6” x 60); SPR per cigar $14.39 Perfecto (5.12 x 60); SRP per cigar $16.99 The Robusto, Toro and Gordo come in 20-count boxes, while the Perfecto comes in a ten-count box. All Room101 Hit & Run packaging features colorful Room101 branding.

Quintessence is the fifth line within Ashton Cigars’ San Cristóbal brand and was preceded by the Revelation, Ovation, Elegancia and original San Cristóbal lines. (For legal reasons, the brand is marketed outside of the US as Paradiso.) Master blender José “Pepin” Garcia from Estelí, Nicaragua, has once again gone above and beyond and created a cigar that we consider the year’s best. Priced at USD $8.00 (EUR 7.40), it also earned our Best Buy rating. The Quintessence line includes four formats: Robusto, Epicure, Majestic and Belicoso. Tasting notes: This perfectly rolled cigar is impressive in its sweetish coffee taste and dried fruit. The fruity notes come into their own wonderfully in the silky smoke. The light peppery spice is stimulating. Medium+. #1 | San Cristóbal (Paradiso) Quintessence Robusto Size: 140 x 19,8 | 5 1/2 x 50 Origin: Nicaragua Wrapper: Ecuador Binder: Nicaragua Filler: Nicaragua Factory: My Father Cigars S.A. Release: 2016

Villiger Cigars announces that the Villiger La Flor De Ynclan will be presented in a special edition Lancero Especial size, at the 2018 IPCPR in Las Vegas this coming July. A cigar- years in the making, Heinrich Villiger and Master Blender Matias Maragoto felt that the best version of the Villiger La Flor De Ynclan had yet to be released. The new Lancero Especial size is described as providing a more intense smoking experience in both flavor and smoke. Only 500, 25 count boxes yearly will be produced for this special edition Lancero Especial vitola. The Villiger La Flor De Ynclan Lancero Especial is a 6 ¾ x 43 with an MSRP of $11.00 Chairman of the Board Heinrich Villiger said, “As I have stated in the past, the Villiger La Flor De Ynclan cigar has been an ongoing labor of love for us, and we feel that we have further refined the blend with the addition of the this special edition lancero vitola. “ About the Villiger La Flor De Ynclan: Diligently crafted by Heinrich Villiger and master blender Jose Matias Maragoto of ABAM Cigar Factory in the Dominican Republic, the Villiger La Flor De Ynlcan was a cigar 10 years in the making. Villiger Cigars produced a small batch of La Flor De Ynclan over a decade ago. Unsatisfied with the final result; the decision was made to cease production. The tobacco was set aside and aged, while Matias meticulously tweaked the amount of the Indonesian, Dominican, and Nicaraguan tobacco within its Ecuadorian wrapper. Present day, the La Flor De Ynclan is what both imagined it could be.

Artesano Del Tobacco is proud to announce that the Viva La Vida Connecticut Churchill began shipping on July 2nd to all retailers who placed pre-orders during the 2026 PCA Trade Show. Following the success of the Viva La Vida Connecticut line, Artesano Del Tobacco is expanding the collection with a new 7 x 54 Churchill vitola. The addition of this size is especially meaningful, as it was developed in direct response to recommendations from the company’s valued retail partners and consumers.“Our clients have always played an important role in helping shape our brands,” said Billy Fakih, Gus Fakih, and Ivan of Artesano Del Tobacco. “We can’t wait for everyone to experience this new Churchill. It took a little longer to bring it to market because we wanted to give the tobacco all the time it needed to develop the flavor profile we envisioned. Working alongside our good friend AJ Fernandez in Estelí, Nicaragua, we created a Churchill that is exceptionally creamy, smooth, naturally sweet, and beautifully balanced. This blend performs incredibly well in this vitola, and we are extremely grateful to everyone who shared their feedback and encouraged us to add this size to the line.” Crafted at AJ Fernandez Cigars in Estelí, Nicaragua, the Viva La Vida Connecticut Churchill features the same blend found throughout the Viva La Vida Connecticut portfolio. It is made with premium Nicaraguan binder and filler tobaccos wrapped in an aged Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper. Product Information * Vitola: Churchill * Size: 7 x 54 * Wrapper: Aged Ecuadorian Connecticut * Binder: Nicaraguan * Filler: Nicaraguan * Factory: AJ Fernandez, Estelí, Nicaragua * Packaging: White wooden boxes of 10 cigars * Suggested Retail Price: $16.00 per cigar

West Tamp Tobacco Company is excited to announce that Chef Rick has begun to ship and will be available both in the US and international markets. Like its predecessors Boliche Blvd. and Devil Crab, Chef Rick serves up a flavorful third course in West Tampa’s food inspired line. “A great culinary chef requires technical mastery, immense passion and creativity” said Rick Rodriguez of the inspiration behind this blend. “I also wanted to take the opportunity to partner with a young up and coming factory, Tabacalera Pages de Nicaragua S.A., to close out this trilogy. Having the opportunity to work along side Raymond Pages Raffo allowed me to bring something new and unique to my fans”, Rodriguez continued. West Tampa Tobacco Company’s Chef Rick will be a limited release of 1,000 boxes, available in one size and packed in a box containing 50 cigars: Toro (6X52)- $12.99 SRP(USD)

At InterTabac, Rick Rodriguez from West Tampa Tobacco introduced his new cigar, Circle of Life. Circle of Life is a story of everyone’s life. The cigar is a medium-strength cigar with a dark wrapper that has been aged for 18 months. An ideal cigar for after dinner. Now available in Robusto (5×52), Toro (6×54), and Gigante (6×60) formats, priced between €18 and €20. Produced at Casa Carrillo in Santiago, Dominican Republic, the cigar is intended to represent the tradition, present, and future of West Tampa. Another new release is the Devil Crab cigar. The cigar is available as a Figurado (4.5×60) and is manufactured by Garmendia Cigar Company in Estelí. West Tampa produces this cigar as a tribute to Tampa’s great cigar history and as a token of appreciation to all those who made this development in Tampa possible. The cigar, which can be enjoyed at any time of day, combines sweetness and delicate spiciness with up to an hour of smoking pleasure. From January 2026, the Figurado will be available at a price of €18 and, in addition to the 20-piece box, also in a 50-piece box.

A limited amount of boxes that have been kept for a decade exclusively for the Spanish market. Tabacalera releases exclusively for the Spanish market a limited batch of Montecristo Open Junior (format “trabuco” 4 1/3 x 38 – 110 mm x 38), that have been aged for ten years in their box. The cigars have been subjected to a decade-long aging in the company’s warehouses, which rounds off the flavor and nuances any edges. The presentation is the same as regular production tobacco, except that a gold sticker has been added to the face of the box, where those ten years of aging stand out. The price of the cigars in stores is 8.50 euros (170 euros for a box of 20), one euro above the regular Montecristo Open Junior.

Tabacalera presents the new edition of Tauromaquia, exclusive for the Spanish market, which pays tribute to the legendary Sevillian bullfighter Juan Belmonte, also known as “El pasmo de Triana”, one of the greatest bullfighters in history. Tauromaquia y Juan Belmonte gives us another opportunity to explore the historical relationship between habanos and bullfighting. Previously, in 2019, the first edition of Tauromaquia was dedicated to Morante de la Puebla and Montecristo Double Edmundo, while in 2020 the protagonists of the second edition were Joselito el Gallo and Partagás Serie P No.2. The brand and vitola chosen for this third edition is Romeo y Julieta Wide Churchills (55 ring gauge x 130 mm long). These cigars have gone through a delicate aging process of at least 5 years, thanks to which the wrappers get slightly darker, smoother and silkier, the flavour settles, and the aroma, strength and body reach a perfect balance. This special edition consists of 1,000 numbered boxes. On the lacquered wooden lid of each box stands out an evocative illustration of the bullfighter. It is available only in Spanish tobacconists at a price of 20 euros/cigar and 200 euros/box of 10 cigars. Info: Romeo y Julieta Wide Churchills, Vitola de galera: Montesco, ring guage 55 (21,83 mm) x 130 mm

The XXV Festival del Habano began with a spectacular opening night. The event celebrated the 150th anniversary of Romeo y Julieta. The exclusive Salón de Protocolo Cubanacán hosted 1,200 guests. Distributors, experts and enthusiasts from all over the world were in attendance. The theme of the evening was Venice, with a romantic atmosphere. The colour red dominated, reflecting the passion of the brand. The new Amantes vitola has a ring gauge of 53 and a length of 153 mm. It was specially designed for the 150th anniversary. The vitola combines tradition with excellent craftsmanship. It offers medium strength and the classic Romeo y Julieta aroma. It is ideal for experienced passionados and newcomers alike. Vice President Jorge Pérez Martel presented two formats: the elegant box of 20 is ideal for collectors and enthusiasts, and an exclusive gift box of 5 was offered in advance to festival guests. The gift box will be available in Switzerland at La Casa del Habano on 17 February 2026 and at Habanos Specialist on 24 February 2026. Romeo y Julieta Amantes – Gift Box with 5 cigars will retail at 372.- Swiss Francs, representing 74.40 Swiss Francs per cigar.

Le Hoyo de San Luis joins the prestigious Le Hoyo Series, celebrated for its aromatic finesse and exeptional craftmanship-hallmarks of the Hoyo de Monterrey brand. Meticulously « Totally Handmade with Long Filler », this new vitola delivers a balanced and smooth smoking experience, featuring leaves exclusively sourced from San Luis, epicenter of tobacco culture in Vuelta Abajo, Pinard el Rio, Cuba. The launch took place on 12 November 2025, during an exclusive dinner show at the famous Alexander Kunz Theatre in Thunstetten, one of Germany`s most exceptional cultural and gastronomic experiences. Presented in boxes of 10, the Le Hoyo de San Luis (Ø52x 160 mm) promises a long and elegant smoking experience, with every draw revealing the refined balance and nuanced character of Hoyo de Monterrey. In Switzerland, they will be available from 21 st of April 2026 at La Casa del Habano stores and from 28th of April 2026 at Habanos Specialist. Le Hoyo de San Luis SLB: 29.03 Swiss Francs per cigar.

A new wooden humidor box with five H. Upmann Magnum 54 cigars is now available in Spanish tobacconists’ shops, standing out as an ideal gift for any Habanos passionado. The Magnum 54 is one of the most emblematic vitolas of the H. Upmann brand. It is a 120 mm long, 54 ring gauge and mild-medium strength vitola. For the final stretch of 2024, this cigar arrives in a special presentation: a new wooden case with a humidifier bearing the brand’s insignia and containing five cigars, already available only in Spanish tobacconists at a price of €120. This is certainly a very interesting idea for those who want to give Habanos as a gift during the upcoming Christmas season, or on any other occasion. H. Upmann is one of the oldest and most prestigious Habanos brands, founded in 1844 by Herman Upmann, a German banker who was also a great lover of Cuban tobacco. The brand is known for its exceptional quality in crafting cigars of mild-medium strength.

Punch Cigars is honoring its iconic (and “devastatingly handsome”) mascot, Mr. Punch, with a new cigar that bears his name. Mr. Punch by Punch Cigars is a full-time blend that delivers a signature Punch smoking experience with a flavor profile tailored to the modern smoker. Mr. Punch by Punch features an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper, a Nicaraguan Jalapa Seco binder, and fillers from Nicaragua. The cigar was produced at the Scandinavian Tobacco Group Factory in Estelí, Nicaragua. Mr. Punch by Punch is available in three sizes: Toro (6 X 54), Gigante (6 X 60), and the largest Punch Cigar ever released, The Big Slapper (7 X 70). SRPs (suggested retail price) for the respective cigars are $7.89, $8.99, and $10.09. Each size is packaged in boxes of 20. Scott Abney, Brand Manager for Punch Cigars, said, “Mr. Punch is a true icon not just in the cigar industry, but in pop culture. So it only made sense to create a cigar that captures his spirit. This new blend delivers a classic Punch smoking experience with a flavor profile tailored to the modern consumer. We know it’s going to be a hit.” Mr. Punch by Punch is a full-time release. It will begin shipping to retailers in July 2026.

After Romeo y Julieta ” Club Kings “, Partagas ” Capitols “, H.Upmann ” Regalias ” and Hoyo de Monterrey ” Souvenir de Luxe “, the Punch brand has also received a Retro Line Habanos edition with the ” Triunfos “. The Petit Corona format has a length of 129 mm and a ring gauge of 42. The tobacco blend comes from the Pinar del Río /Vuelta Abajo region and scores points with its leaf selection. The “Souvenir de Luxe” is rolled into a soft cigar with a light, fruity and honey-like taste. The light taste of its blend is an attractive alternative for those who like a light, tasty and aromatic Habano with elegance and complexity. Suitable as a permanent guest. The Punch “Triunfos” is offered in a color-coordinated aluminum box in retro design with 5 cigars. They will be available from 05.03.2024 in the Swiss Casa del Habano and from 12.03.2024 in Habanos Specialist stores. Punch Triunfos, tin of 5 cigars, has a RSP of CHF 80.-

Serie Sevilla is the name of a collection, exclusive to the Spanish market, of Habanos cigars presented in English earthenware jars. The jars, made by “La Cartuja de Sevilla”, are a replica of those made by the same firm in the middle of the last century for the Partagás and Ramón Allones brands, which are now genuine museum pieces. The first edition of Serie Sevilla, produced in 2016, featured Montecristo No.3, followed in 2017 by Hoyo de Monterrey Epicure Especial, H. Upmann Magnum 50 in 2018, Partagás Serie P No.2 in 2019, Romeo y Julieta Short Churchills in 2020 and Ramón Allones Allones Specially Selected in 2021. This 7 th edition consists of 1,000 numbered pieces. Each of them contains 21 Únicos, the brand’s Pirámides (156 mm in length and 52 filler), entirely hand-rolled and preserved in the best conditions. It is priced at €25 per cigar and €525 per box.

Launched in 1996, Vegueros was born to pay homage to all the Cuban farmers who, from generation to generation, have grown tobacco in Pinar del Río*. The place where the Vegueros brand is made today is the Rolling Tobacco Factory “Francisco Donatien,” a solid building in Pinar del Río* built in 1868 and which became a tobacco factory in 1961. The brand, which completely renewed itself more than fifteen years after its creation by adding innovative formats to its portfolio, now enriches the range with the CentroGordos vitola (54 ring gauge x 100 mm length), an attractive option for those looking for a Habano with a medium to strong flavor, accessible and renewed. Vegueros CentroGordos is presented with the new brand image and in a 16-unit metal can. It is a trendy format, much appreciated by smokers these days and will be accessible to a broader spectrum of smokers. All the Habanos of this brand are made “Totalmente a mano con tripa larga” – Totally Handmade with Long Filler -, with a medium to full flavour. Vegueros Centrogordos will be available in Switzerland on the 24 th of October 2023 in the Casa del Habano and on the 31 st in the Habanos Specialist stores. The box of Vegueros Centrogordo of 16 cigars is proposed to a RSP of 142.40 Swiss Francs.
